faq.q: What does the dot product mean?
faq.a: It measures how much two vectors point the same way, times their sizes. Big and positive means they agree, zero means they are at right angles, negative means they point against each other.

faq.q: Why is the dot product zero for perpendicular vectors?
faq.a: At 90 degrees, one vector casts no shadow on the other, and cos 90 degrees is 0. So the product is 0.
asks: Why does a dot b equal 0 at right angles?

faq.q: How do you calculate a dot product?
faq.a: Multiply matching parts and add. For a equals 2, 3 and b equals 4, 1, the dot product is 2 times 4 plus 3 times 1, which is 11. Or use size times size times cos theta.
asks: How do I work out a dot b?

faq.q: How do you find the angle between two vectors?
faq.a: Rearrange: cos theta equals a dot b divided by the size of a times the size of b. Then use inverse cosine.
asks: How do I use the dot product to find an angle?

faq.q: Where is the dot product used?
faq.a: In physics, work done is force dot displacement. In computer graphics it decides how bright a surface looks. In machine learning it measures how similar two lists of numbers are.
asks: What is the dot product used for?

facts: a·b = |a||b|cos θ, where θ is the angle between the vectors.
Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular exactly when their dot product is 0.
